_source: AI-researched venue CANDIDATES for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly edited by the research agent. Populated by a daily scheduled research agent (2026-08, at explicit user request: 'fan out some research agents who's goal is to run every day to find and suggest new businesses... they shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet'; bumped from ~3-5/day to 10/day at a later explicit request). See .claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md for the full research brief/rules this agent works under (Hard rule 1 chain/fast-food screening, real coordinates only, no duplicates, Do/Drink/Eat coverage balance). The research agent commits straight to master for this file (no PR — this queue has zero effect on the live app, nothing reads it except the review agent and the admin dashboard's Growth Insights context). A second, independent daily agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) re-verifies each `pending` entry and is the thing that promotes one into the real docs/data/venues.json, pushing straight to master after its own independent re-verification (see that file's own 2026-09-04 doc comment for why the human checkpoint moved to Curia Command's Pending Review tab instead of a PR here). Each entry mirrors docs/data/venues.json's own raw shape (name/district/type/spend/lat/lon/base/bands/reason) exactly, so a reviewed-and-approved entry can be moved into that file with a straight copy-paste, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) that get stripped on promotion. `district` values must be a real existing district id from docs/data/districts.json (manchester/cheshire metros only) UNLESS the entry is itself proposing a brand-new district — see district-suggestions.json for that case instead; a venue suggestion should never invent a district id that doesn't exist anywhere.
_reviewWorkflow: status starts 'pending' on every new entry. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent changes it to 'approved'/promoted (then copies the venue fields into docs/data/venues.json and removes the entry here, pushed straight to master) or 'rejected' (left here with researchNotes explaining why, as a record so the same candidate isn't re-suggested later — curia-research-daily checks every entry here regardless of status before suggesting anything new). Genuinely uncertain candidates go to docs/data/pending-review-queue.json instead, staying 'pending' here until a human decides via Curia Command. A human's actual review happens by reading Curia Command's daily briefing and Pending Review tab, not by editing this file directly, though a human reviewer (or a future admin-dashboard screen) can still hand-edit an entry's status here if needed.

suggestions.name: Clark Art
suggestions.reason: Bill Clark's own gallery on Ashley Road since 1999, deep in L.S. Lowry and the northern painters he's written the books on — a private dealer's eye, not a gallery chain's algorithm.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Clark Art (155 Ashley Road, Hale) closed permanently on 3 October 2024 after 18 years, per Bill Clark's own retirement announcement (reported by Altrincham Today, 'An incredible journey: Clark Art to close after 18 years in Hale village'). The prior research pass's sources (Tripadvisor/Artsy/halebarns.com listings) were stale directory pages that hadn't been updated to reflect the closure. Do not re-suggest — the gallery no longer exists.

suggestions.name: Yang Sing
suggestions.reason: Three floors of a Grade II-listed Princess Street townhouse, family-run since the 1970s — bottomless yum cha that still draws a queue nobody seems to mind.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Yang Sing (34 Princess Street) has been closed since December 2021/early 2022 (kitchen fire, then a lease dispute) and Yang Sing Limited is now in liquidation per Companies House — it never reopened despite the owner's 2022 hope to reopen by 2023/24. The prior research pass's sources (visitmanchester.com, Hardens, Tripadvisor) were stale listings still showing it as an open, operating restaurant. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Blue Lobster
suggestions.reason: Italian seafood on the corner of London Road and Brown Street, sourced directly from Rome — a Franciacorta bar downstairs, the kitchen running until midnight upstairs.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Blue Lobster (34 London Road, Alderley Edge) closed permanently in December 2017, less than nine months after its April 2017 opening, following a staff-payment dispute with owner Andrea Zecchino (reported by alderleyedge.com and Manchester Confidential at the time). No evidence of any reopening or trading activity was found in the eight years since. The prior research pass's Tripadvisor/Luxury Lifestyle Magazine sources were leftover listings from the 2017 opening, not current confirmation. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Fire Station Social Cucina
suggestions.reason: A pizza theatre and wood oven where Gusto used to sit on London Road — hand-rolled pasta, Napoli-style bases, and only one other room anywhere doing the same thing.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via thebusinessdesk.com, wilmslow.co.uk/alderleyedge.com and the operator's own site (firestationsocial.co.uk): Fire Station Social Cucina, 75 London Road, Alderley Edge SK9 7DY, opened 10 June 2026 in the former Gusto unit — the second site for this specific concept, after the original in Tarporley. Run by 'Project Social Cucina', the restaurant division of Cheshire Pub Company (a separate entity from the 7-pub Cheshire Cat group already referenced elsewhere in this file) — only 2 sites confirmed under the Fire Station Social Cucina name itself, the same 2-site sibling precedent already used for Cibo/Suburban Green/Smoke Wilmslow/Heddy's/Caramello. Flagged for the reviewer: the parent company's own press describes this as 'expansion', so worth a quick re-check at promotion time that a third site hasn't since appeared. Moderate-high confidence otherwise — real, recently opened, well-covered locally, no closure signals. Re-checked again 2026-09-08 (curia-suggestion-review daily pass) specifically for a rumoured third site: none found — same 2-site status as this note originally recorded, still pending, still in docs/data/pending-review-queue.json for a human call rather than re-decided here. DECIDED 2026-09-08 by direct user instruction, in an interactive session: promoted into venues.json with the new `status: 'coming-soon'` field (added the same day specifically for this case) rather than a flat yes/no — real venue, passes Hard rule 1 on site count today, but its editorial confidence marker stays provisional given the parent's stated expansion plans. See venues.json's own note on the new field.

suggestions.name: The Copper Room
suggestions.reason: Amy and Rick Armstrong crowdfunded their way into Charles Roe House's Grade II* rooms — steak and seafood cooked properly, in a silk merchant's own dining room on Chestergate.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the operator's own site (chefrick.co.uk), Macclesfield Nub News (two separate pieces confirming both the Kickstarter-funded opening and the venue name) and Tripadvisor (active listing with 2026-dated reviews): The Copper Room, Charles Roe House, 60-62 Chestergate, Macclesfield SK11 6DY, a fine-dining restaurant and cocktail bar run by chef-owners Amy and Rick Armstrong. No second site or group ownership found anywhere — single-site, independently owned, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from doogal.co.uk's postcode geocode for SK11 6DY. Reuses the existing FINE DINING type. Fills a real gap: Macclesfield had only 1 Eat-category venue (Chestergate Bistro) against 2 Do and 3 Drink before this addition. REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-14: the chef-owned fine-dining concept this candidate described no longer trades at 60-62 Chestergate. Charles Roe House's dining room changed to 'Piccante at The Copper Room' (Italian/Brazilian tapas, opened Dec 2022) and per Macclesfield Nub News that room has sat empty since summer 2025 while the building is converted into a different, unrelated venture, 'The Charles Roe Pub' (reopening Dec 2025). Amy and Rick Armstrong's ownership story checks out, but whatever they run today is not trading at this address under this description — a closure/identity mismatch, not a chain issue. Do not re-suggest at this address; a genuinely reopened Armstrong-run venue elsewhere would need its own fresh verification.

suggestions.name: Prana
suggestions.reason: Two floors of proper acoustics on Ashley Road from the team behind Stockport's Amp — order the cocktail, but the stage is the reason to stay past nine.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-22: Google Maps marks it 'Permanently closed' (posting disabled), its own site returns a dead Cloudflare error, Instagram/Facebook are gone, Skiddle shows zero events ever listed, and its sister venue (Amp, Stockport) also closed and reopened under an unrelated name/concept. The property itself (14-16 Ashley Road) is listed for sale as former restaurant premises. Companies House shows an 'Active' shell (PRANA F&B LIMITED) with overdue first accounts — not evidence of an operating business. Do not re-suggest.

suggestions.name: Mouro Coffee Bar
suggestions.reason: Moroccan tile underfoot and a La Marzocco machine doing the actual work — focaccia sandwiches, matcha and affogato for a stretch of Heaton Moor Road that doesn't need to shout about any of it.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Tripadvisor (5.0/5, current 2026 listing), the Food Standards Agency ratings register and the venue's own Instagram (@mourocoffeebar): Mouro Coffee Bar, 72 Heaton Moor Road, Stockport SK4 4NZ — a design-led independent coffee bar serving speciality coffee, cold-pressed juices, pastries and focaccia sandwiches. No second site or group ownership found anywhere despite a direct search; single-site, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from postcode geocode for SK4 4NZ. Reuses the existing BRUNCH SPOT type. Heaton Moor was at 8 venues (3 Do, 3 Drink, 2 Eat) before this addition — Eat was its thinnest category, and the district is one of ten currently under the 10-venue standing target. High confidence. REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-16: the 'no second site found anywhere' claim doesn't hold up — Mouro is in fact a real, actively expanding four-site coffee brand: the original Heaton Moor site, two Altrincham sites (25 Market Street and 8-10 Oxford Road, opened August 2025), and a fourth opened 16 May 2026 on Tib Street in the Northern Quarter itself (themanc.com's own coverage explicitly headlines it 'Mouro opens third coffee shop', undercounting even by its own count since two Altrincham sites exist). This is well past this file's established 2-3-site small-sibling-group allowance and spans two separate towns plus a city-centre expansion — a real, currently-growing chain by Hard rule 1's own standard, not a family pair. Do not re-suggest unless the brand's footprint materially contracts.

suggestions.name: Underbank
suggestions.reason: A former bank branch turned beer hall and soundsystem room at the crossroads of the two Underbanks — Pomona Island and Runaway on tap, and a rig loud enough that conversation moves to the beer garden after ten.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-22: investigated as a suspected name/identity mismatch with the existing 'The Underbank' catalog entry (same building, 27 Great Underbank). Found no evidence a second real venue exists — the theory traced to a January 2025 Instagram announcement (Benji Taylor's own plan for a live-music venue in the same building) that appears to have been superseded by what actually opened in May 2025 (the O'Malleys' 'The Underbank', which itself runs gigs/comedy/quiz nights, not just a beer hall). The existing catalog entry's name and core facts are correct as-is. Do not re-suggest as a separate venue without direct on-the-ground confirmation.

suggestions.name: Olive Tree Brasserie
suggestions.reason: Meze and a bottomless brunch on Watergate Row since 2016 — Dean Wilson's third room, not his first draft, and it still runs on a Greek kitchen's own instincts.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-22: the original candidate's '3rd site, Lytham/Preston/Chester' framing understated the real scale — the group's own site today lists FOUR active locations (Chester, Leeds, Lytham, Stockton Heath) across three counties, plus a closed 5th site (Preston, liquidated 2021). Founder/director Dean Wilson was disqualified from running any company for 10.5 years in Nov 2024 after fraudulently claiming ~£200k in COVID Bounce Back Loans across the group's per-site companies. A genuine multi-city regional chain, not a small group — do not re-suggest.

suggestions.name: Bali Health Lounge
suggestions.reason: Three floors above George Street built around ELEMIS facials and a tea lounge — Chinatown's actual quiet room, one flight up from everything loud below it.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-22, overturning an earlier 'moderate-high confidence, still trading' read: the operating company (Bali Health Lounge Limited, #07411581, same address) passed a creditors' voluntary liquidation resolution in Dec 2022 and was formally dissolved 4 Dec 2024 (The Gazette, Companies House). The 'live' Yelp/Tripadvisor activity that misled the earlier pass is uncurated listing pages carrying stale marketing copy with auto-generated 'Updated' headers regardless of actual status — no genuinely-dated 2023-2026 review or evidence of a relaunch was found. Do not re-suggest unless a new operator/relaunch is confirmed.

suggestions.name: The Nest Nantwich
suggestions.reason: Nick Wadeson's own copper still, Valerie, still runs on Pepper Street — the family behind Three Wrens Gin poured their production room into a proper cocktail bar rather than settling for a tasting counter.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED — exact duplicate of a venue already live in docs/data/venues.json under the identical name and coordinates (a different real venue on Pepper Street, Nantwich, already catalogued as a cocktail bar with its own working still). The pipeline's dedup logic only checks this suggestions file, not venues.json itself, so it missed the collision. Do not re-suggest.

suggestions.name: Amici
suggestions.reason: Italian-Greek tapas in the Village Square, run by Andrea, Giovanni and Chris on a menu that never quite picks a country — steak and seafood mains for whoever wants to stop sharing.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED — exact duplicate of a venue already live in docs/data/venues.json under the identical name, district and coordinates (Bramhall, Italian-Greek tapas, Andrea/Giovanni/Chris). Same dedup gap as The Nest Nantwich/Amazing India in this same batch. Do not re-suggest.

suggestions.name: Amazing India
suggestions.reason: Joby Joy's South Indian room on Pickford Street, the only one of its kind in town — dosas and a party hall that means the celebration doesn't have to end when the curry does.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED — exact duplicate of a venue already live in docs/data/venues.json under the identical name, district and near-identical coordinates (Macclesfield, South Indian, Pickford Street). Same dedup gap as The Nest Nantwich/Amici in this same batch. Do not re-suggest.

suggestions.name: King Street Kitchen
suggestions.reason: Small, family-run, and on King Street since long before the brunch queue started forming outside it — a plant-based option on every course, not just the one everyone else bothers with.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED — this venue was already investigated, confirmed closed (two independent listing sites marking it CLOSED, corroborated by a local Facebook post) and removed from docs/data/venues.json on 2026-09-08 (see docs/data/pending-review-queue.json's own record of that decision). The daily research pipeline re-suggested it again on 2026-09-22 without checking that history — a real dedup gap (this file's own dedup logic only checks entries within this file, not venues.json's removal/closure history). Do not re-suggest; if the pipeline's dedup logic gets fixed, this is the case that should have caught it.

suggestions.name: Mobberley Brewhouse Tap & Shop
suggestions.reason: The brewery's original building on Church Lane, kept on as a tap and shop once production moved up the road to bigger premises — sample the cans standing among the old fermenters, then take a few home for whoever couldn't make the drive.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via CAMRA/whatpub.com, Great British Life ('Local life — Mobberley Tap & Shop') and Untappd (check-ins as recent as August 2026, confirming current trading): Mobberley Brewhouse Tap & Shop, Dairy Farm, Church Lane, Mobberley WA16 7RA — the original site of Mobberley Brewhouse, kept running as a taproom and bottle/can shop after brewing production relocated to larger premises on Woodend Lane. Open tap nights are held the first Tuesday of each month. No second tap/shop site found anywhere in searches; single independent brewery, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from the WA16 7RA postcode centroid (web geocode search, doogal.co.uk blocked this session). Reuses the existing BREWERY TAP type (introduced same-day for the RedWillow, Macclesfield candidate elsewhere in this file). Real Drink gap this closes: Mobberley's three real Drink-mapped venues (The Bull's Head, Church Inn, Railway Inn) are all COUNTRY PUB — this is a genuinely different register (a working brewery's own taproom, not a pub kitchen). Note for the reviewer: two other well-known Mobberley pubs (Church Inn, Bull's Head) already live in venues.json are, per fresh research this run, both actually part of the 7-strong Cheshire Cat Pubs & Bars group (Tim Bird/Mary McLaughlin) — flagging for awareness/spot-check since that group's scale sits at the edge of this file's own precedent, though not something this candidate depends on. High confidence on Mobberley Brewhouse itself — small, single-site, well-documented, current 2026 activity confirmed. REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-29: the candidate's own research described only the original Mobberley tap/shop plus a larger production site up the road, framed as a small single-sibling case. Fresh search this run found Mobberley Brewhouse (MBH) has since also opened taproom sites in Knutsford and Stockport ('Project 53' on Stockport Market Place) — three real, separate public taproom locations across three different towns under one brand, not a two-site pair. This crosses the same threshold that sank Mouro Coffee Bar in this file's own history (a real, currently-expanding multi-town chain by the brand's own site count, not a family pair) — distinct from RedWillow's accepted 2-town/2-site Macclesfield+Buxton pattern precisely because a third town has now been added. Do not re-suggest unless the brand's footprint materially contracts back to two sites.

suggestions.name: Cask & Kiln
suggestions.reason: Two former Black Dog barmen took a unit on Wilbraham Road and filled it with sixty-odd drams — whisky flights for whoever's had enough of Chorlton's usual pint.
suggestions.researchNotes: Chorlton's real Drink category (The Chorlton Tap, The Beer House, The Jane Eyre Chorlton, plus The Creameries' dual-mapped GASTROPUB) is all ale-house/cocktail-bar register — no whisky-led venue. Verified via Manchester Wire ('New bar: Cask and Kiln whiskey & craft beer bar in Chorlton'), Confidentials ('Cask & Kiln - Chorlton's new whisky bar opens Friday') and Ginfuelledbluestocking's own opening write-up: Cask & Kiln, 478 Wilbraham Road, Chorlton-cum-Hardy, Manchester M21 9AS — founded by Aaron Wood and Jack Foster-Currie, former employees of the Black Dog Beer House group, stocking over 60 whiskies alongside craft beer. No second site or group ownership found anywhere in searches (specifically checked given the founders' Black Dog background — that's their former employer, not a current ownership tie); single-site, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates (53.4420/-2.2810) approximated along Wilbraham Road between the already-catalogued Dulcimer (567 Wilbraham Road, 53.4428/-2.2735) and Chorlton's town centre, since doogal.co.uk/api.postcodes.io were both blocked this session — flagged for the reviewer to tighten. New use of the existing WHISKY BAR type (introduced 2026-09-18 for a different Manchester venue), reused here rather than a new type. High confidence on the venue itself — well-documented opening across multiple independent local outlets, current, no closure signals; the coordinate approximation is the one flag. REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-29: the candidate's own sources (Manchester Wire, Confidentials, ginfuelledbluestocking) describing a 'new' whisky bar opening are genuinely dated to October 2017, not a 2026 opening as the suggestion implied — CAMRA/whatpub and Yelp confirm Cask & Kiln at 478 Wilbraham Road actually closed in 2019/2020, and the address is now occupied by an unrelated, currently-trading restaurant (Yara, Lebanese & Syrian). A real venue once existed at this address under this name, but it does not exist today — do not re-suggest unless a genuinely new whisky bar reopens there under current ownership.

suggestions.name: Bottle
suggestions.reason: Ten taps and a suntrap garden on Shaw Road since 2015 — Corin Bland's own shop, open years before he took on the Market Hall's beer hall in town, and still the one worth sitting down in.
suggestions.researchNotes: Re-tallied Manchester/Cheshire district/category coverage against the current venues.json + pending/approved suggestions before researching (script-assisted, CATEGORY_BY_VENUE_TYPE applied, filtered to manchester/cheshire districts only per this run's own scope note). Heaton Moor's real mapped Drink category was the thinnest found this run (Heaton Social, Cork of the North — Beer Shop's BOTTLE SHOP type doesn't get a second real example) even after accounting for the still-pending Thom's Bar & Kitchen candidate. Verified via CAMRA (camra.org.uk/pubs/bottle-heaton-moor-heaton-moor-167107), whatpub.com and Stockport & South Manchester CAMRA's own writeup: Bottle, 9a Shaw Road, Heaton Moor SK4 4AG — opened 3 April 2015 in former shop premises by Corin Bland, founder of the earlier High Peak Beer Co. in Stockport Market Hall; 10 beer taps, an extensive cans/bottles range, a 15-seat beer garden. Corin Bland's other venture (High Peak Beer Co., Stockport Market Hall, Underbanks district) is a real second site under the same founder but a different name/brand in a different district of the same metro — within this file's own small-sibling-across-districts precedent (Nam/Ōdiobā), flagged for the reviewer regardless. No third site found anywhere. Coordinates (53.4232/-2.1855) from a direct postcode search for SK4 4AG (checkmypostcode.uk, api.postcodes.io/doogal.co.uk both blocked this session) — matches the same tight Heaton Moor town-centre cluster as this district's other already-catalogued venues. Reuses the existing BOTTLE SHOP type (Beer Heroes, Chester; Beer Shop, also Heaton Moor — a second, distinct bottle shop on a different street is a real and reasonable overlap, not a duplicate). High confidence — over a decade of continuous trading, well-documented, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: Convene
suggestions.reason: Isabella Cubrilo swapped her Balkan Bible supper club for a permanent stove on Lower Hillgate — a seasonal menu that changes before regulars get bored of it, and a coffee counter that means nobody's just passing through.
suggestions.researchNotes: Stockport (Underbanks)'s real mapped Eat category was tied for this run's thinnest cell (Where the Light Gets In, Bar Caput, Kambuja — 3 real Eat-mapped venues before this addition, Sticky Fingers Bakery's BAKERY type not currently reused for a second Eat entry here). Verified via manchestersfinest.com ('Convene'), confidentials.com ('Lower Hillgate's new hotspot: Convene, Stockport, reviewed'), stockport.nub.news ('New neighbourhood cafe opens in Stockport town centre') and scoresonthedoors.org.uk (Food Hygiene Rating 5, awarded 8 July 2026, confirming current trading): Convene, 17 Lower Hillgate, Stockport SK1 1JQ — opened 6 March 2026, run by chef Isabella Cubrilo (previously head chef at Altrincham's à bloc, and behind the 'Balkan Bible' supper club series), a neighbourhood cafe built around specialty coffee and a weekly-changing seasonal menu, open Tue-Sat 8am-4pm and Sun 9am-4pm (closed Monday) — daytime only, no evening service found in any source checked. No second site found anywhere in searches; a separate 'Convene SK Ltd' Companies House entry (incorporated Dec 2025, registered at a different Stockport address) may be a related holding company but no second trading site was found under it. Passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates (53.4103/-2.1558) from a direct postcode search for SK1 1JQ (checkmypostcode.uk; api.postcodes.io/doogal.co.uk both blocked this session). Typed BRUNCH SPOT (matching Idle Hands/Aldeli's daytime-cafe register) rather than COFFEE ROOM, since the seasonal-cooking food menu is as central to the venue as the coffee. High confidence — well-documented recent opening across multiple independent local outlets, current food hygiene rating, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: Maricarmen
suggestions.reason: José Núñez's tapas started as a Friday-night pop-up inside an Ancoats chocolate shop before it earned its own address — the queue moved with it, and a second room in the Northern Quarter hasn't thinned it out.
suggestions.researchNotes: Ancoats' real mapped Eat category (Erst, Mana, Pollen Bakery, Indian Affair — 4 venues) was among this run's thinnest, and the district's own pending Butter Bird candidate uses a new, not-yet-wired ROTISSERIE type, so doesn't count toward CATEGORY_BY_VENUE_TYPE coverage yet. Verified via manchestersfinest.com, Tripadvisor (active, current 2026 listing), manchestertime.co.uk and themanc.com ('Manc tapas spot Maricarmen open second site in Northern Quarter'): Maricarmen, 67 Great Ancoats Street, Manchester M4 5AB — chef José Núñez's Spanish tapas restaurant, which began as a pop-up inside an Ancoats chocolatier before securing this permanent site in 2023. A second Maricarmen site has since opened in the Northern Quarter (with a further in-house 'Gildas by Maricarmen' concept at that site, not a third separate address) — a real 2-site pair, both within Manchester itself, within this file's own established small-sibling-in-the-same-metro precedent (Little Tap/Terrarium, Nam/Ōdiobā). No third site found anywhere. Coordinates (53.4834/-2.22973) for 67 Great Ancoats Street found via direct web search rather than a postcode approximation. Reuses the existing SMALL PLATES type (Erst, Australasia). Moderate-high confidence — well-documented across multiple independent local outlets, current, no closure signals; the 2-site footprint is the one flag worth a second look at promotion time.

suggestions.name: Dahlia Stereo
suggestions.reason: Open-fire barbacoa on the ground floor, a mezcal and tequila liquorita built into the bar itself, and a sound system upstairs curated by two Manchester DJs who never needed the introduction — dinner doesn't have to end when the plates do.
suggestions.researchNotes: Northern Quarter's real mapped Eat category (BAB NQ, Evelyn's Cafe Bar, Idle Hands, This & That — 4 venues) is genuinely thin against its own Do (7) and Drink (9), the same imbalance this run's tile-catalog tally flagged (the still-pending Smaak candidate uses a new, not-yet-wired DUTCH FRY HOUSE type, so doesn't count toward this yet). Verified via manchesterwire.co.uk ('Dahlia: New two-floor Latin BBQ restaurant & bar', 'Dahlia Stereo brings big-name DJs and barbacoa dining'), manchestersfinest.com, ilovemanchester.com and themanc.com: Dahlia Stereo, Units 1 & 2, The Hive, 47 Lever Street, Manchester M1 1FN — opened 10 September 2026 in the former Pie & Ale unit, from WANT Studios (Andy Marshall, Andy Windsor, Liam McCue, Adelaide Winter), the creative hospitality studio previously behind Manchester venues Ramona and The Firehouse. Three concepts under one roof: Barbacoa Cósmica (an open-fire grill kitchen, Latin American and southern-US inspired), Bar Más Bonita (a tequila/mezcal/rum-focused liquorita at the bar's centre) and Dahlia Stereo itself (a music-first space with a bespoke sound system, programmed by Jonjo Williams of Maribou State and Rich Reason of Hit & Run). Flagged explicitly for the review agent: this is WANT Studios' third Manchester venue (Ramona, The Firehouse, now Dahlia) — a real local footprint worth a second look, though all three sit in Manchester itself, the same shape as other small local groups already accepted in this file (Dukes Hospitality's 5 Macclesfield bars, The Salt House's 3 Northwich sites) rather than a multi-city chain. Coordinates (53.4831/-2.2333) for 47 Lever Street/The Hive found via direct web search. Typed SMOKEHOUSE (Eat) — the open-fire cooking is the more distinctive, less-covered register versus another cocktail bar, and closes the real Eat gap this run's tally found — over LIVE MUSIC BAR, which would have added to Drink instead, already Northern Quarter's thickest category. Moderate-high confidence — very recently opened so less review history than an established venue, but well-documented by multiple independent local outlets with no closure signal (nothing yet to close); the 3-venue local ownership footprint is the one flag worth a second look at promotion time.

suggestions.name: One Thirty Cafe & Bar
suggestions.reason: A family-run counter on Hulme Hall Road that pours prosecco and bottled beer alongside the flat whites — Cheadle Hulme's daytime answer to a proper bar, gone by mid-afternoon rather than staying open just to prove a point.
suggestions.researchNotes: Cheadle Hulme's real mapped Drink category (Archive Bar & Bottle, Inventery, The Chiverton Tap's dual ALE HOUSE mapping — 3 venues) was this run's single thinnest Drink cell alongside Prestbury's. Researched several Cheadle Hulme options first and rejected them on Hard rule 1: Ye Olde Admiral Rodney (a genuine Robinsons Brewery tied house, part of a ~200-pub regional estate) and The Station House (reopened 2025 under Almond Family Pubs/Joseph Holt, a managed multi-site pub group) both fail the chain-footprint check cleanly. Verified via Tripadvisor (multiple current reviews describing it as 'a small independent coffee shop', one noting a change of ownership 'in December' with the business continuing to trade under new management) and independent listing sites: One Thirty Cafe & Bar, 130 Hulme Hall Road, Cheadle Hulme, Stockport SK8 6LQ — family-run, licensed to serve wine, prosecco and bottled beer alongside coffee, tea and milkshakes; open Mon-Fri 8am-2:30pm, Sat 9am-2pm, Sun 10am-1:30pm — a genuinely daytime venue, no evening trading found in any source. No second site or group ownership found anywhere in searches; single-site, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates (53.3667/-2.19) from a direct postcode search for SK8 6LQ (checkmypostcode.uk; api.postcodes.io/doogal.co.uk both blocked this session) — this sits toward the southern edge of Cheadle Hulme's known venue spread (close to Thorn Grove Park's own coordinates), flagged for the reviewer to confirm it's genuinely within the district rather than bordering Cheadle proper. Typed COFFEE ROOM (Drink, 'Cafés (late)' tile) rather than a bar type, since its own hours don't extend past early afternoon. Moderate confidence — real, licensed, currently trading per recent reviews, but a smaller, lower-profile business than a dedicated bar, and the ownership-change detail is the one thing worth a second look at promotion time.

suggestions.name: Prestbury Farm Shop
suggestions.reason: Free-range game and fish landed that morning, sold from the same corner of The Village for longer than most of Prestbury's restaurants have existed — the village's actual larder, not a gift-shop version of one.
suggestions.researchNotes: Prestbury's real mapped Drink category (Bacchus, The Foxhole — 2 venues, the champagne-bar/cocktail-bar register only) was this run's other single thinnest Drink cell alongside Cheadle Hulme's. No genuinely new, unduplicated, non-chain Drink candidate was found for Prestbury this run despite several searches — Ye Olde Admiral Rodney (Robinsons Brewery tied house) was the only real lead and fails Hard rule 1 on chain footprint; per this run's own 'when genuinely unsure, drop the candidate' standard, nothing was forced into that gap. This candidate instead closes a different real gap found in the same research pass: Prestbury has no FARM SHOP-type venue despite two of its Cheshire neighbours (Mobberley's Waugh Brow, Tarporley's The Hollies/Rose Farm Shop) already having one. Verified via bigbarn.co.uk, the operator's own Facebook page and Companies House (PRESTBURY'S FARM SHOP LTD, company 07347353): Prestbury Farm Shop, 1 The Village, Prestbury, Macclesfield SK10 4DG — an independent farm shop selling free-range game, fine meats, fresh fish and locally produced fruit and vegetables. No second site or group ownership found anywhere in searches; single-site, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates (53.2893/-2.1516) match this district's own already-seeded SK10 4DG-area venues (Bacchus, The Legh Arms, Rococo, The Foxhole, Henry's Cafe, Prestbury Cricket Club all share this same postcode centroid in this file already), so this sits squarely within the same village-centre cluster. Reuses the existing FARM SHOP type (Waugh Brow Farm Shop, Mobberley). Moderate-high confidence — well-documented long-standing trading, no closure signals; the Drink gap this run set out to close remains open and is flagged here rather than papered over.

suggestions.name: Libero
suggestions.reason: Sixteen seats and a craft-only tap list in a Kings Court unit the size of a front room — Rooney's been running it long enough that the football crowd never had to be told twice where to go.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via manchestersfinest.com, CAMRA (camra.org.uk/pubs/libero-altrincham-129878), pelliclemag.com and manchesterwire.co.uk ('Libero team announce plans and launch crowdfunder for new Sale bar'): Libero, 2A Kings Court, Railway Street, Altrincham WA14 2RE — a tiny (16-seat), independent craft-beer-only sports bar, founded by 'Rooney' more than six years ago, described consistently as one of Altrincham's most-loved small independents. The same team is opening a second, differently-named venue (Pray Tell, natural wine and cocktails) in Sale's Stanley Square — a real second site under the same team but a different brand/concept/town, outside Curia's Manchester/Cheshire district list (Sale has no district here), flagged for the reviewer as a footprint worth a second look rather than treated as disqualifying on its own, within this file's small-sibling precedent. No other Libero site found anywhere. Coordinates (53.3851/-2.3518) from a direct postcode search for WA14 2RE (checkmypostcode.uk; api.postcodes.io/doogal.co.uk both blocked this session). Typed ALE HOUSE (matching its craft-beer-only, no-frills register) rather than SPORTS BAR, no equivalent of which exists in the current catalogue. Altrincham's real Drink category (Porta, Riddles, HARCOURT's dual mapping, Gin Can) is workable but entirely cocktail/sherry-bar/gastropub register — Libero is a genuinely different, more down-to-earth kind of Drink venue. High confidence — six years of continuous, well-documented independent trading, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: A.T. Welch
suggestions.reason: Walk through the working pork butcher's counter to find the café at the back — fourth-generation Austins, a replica 1940s grocery still standing behind it, and a full breakfast served on china that's never once been swapped for paper plates.
suggestions.researchNotes: Nantwich's real mapped Eat category (Basmati, Deadwood Smokehouse — 2 venues; Residence and Bench Bistro Bar's BISTRO type isn't currently wired into CATEGORY_BY_VENUE_TYPE) was one of this run's thinnest Eat cells despite Nantwich's real total venue count sitting comfortably above 10. Verified via greatbritishlife.co.uk ('A.T. Welch — the Nantwich butcher's shop carving a future from the past'), Tripadvisor (active, current 2026 listing and reviews) and Yell/restaurantguru.com: A.T. Welch, 45 Hospital Street, Nantwich CW5 5RL — a traditional pork butcher, delicatessen and coffee shop run by Roger and Stuart Austin, the fourth generation of their family in the grocery trade, with a preserved 1940s grocery-shop display inside; serves breakfast, brunch, lunch and afternoon tea. No second site or group ownership found anywhere in searches; single-site, family-owned, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. High confidence — long-established multi-generation family business, well-documented, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: Colin Jellicoe Gallery
suggestions.reason: Sixty years of the same independent eye on Portland Street, still hanging shows the gallery's late founder would have approved of — one of the longest-running galleries in the city, and one of the quietest.
suggestions.researchNotes: Chinatown's real Do category (Manchester Art Gallery, Contemporary Six, T.La Art & Craft Gallery — all 3 real venues are art galleries, no other register) was this run's thinnest real Do cell alongside Mobberley's; no non-gallery Do candidate was found for Chinatown despite several searches (spa/tea-shop leads found were either already-pending duplicates in register — Siamease Thai Spa, Ohayo Tea — or, for Woo Tea, a 2-site cross-city expansion from an original London site judged too uncertain a footprint to add alongside an already-pending same-register candidate). Verified via the gallery's own site (colinjellicoe.co.uk) and Tripadvisor (current, active listing with published hours): Colin Jellicoe Gallery, 82 Portland Street, Manchester M1 4QX — founded by painter Colin Jellicoe, moved to this Portland Street address in a partnership with Alan Behar in 1968; one of Manchester's longest continuously-running independent galleries, still trading today (open Tue-Fri 12-5pm, Sat 1-5pm) after Jellicoe's death in 2018. No second site or group ownership found anywhere in searches; single-site, independently owned, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates (53.4782/-2.2393) found via direct web search for the Portland Street address — this sits at Chinatown's northern edge toward Piccadilly Gardens rather than its Faulkner Street/George Street core, the same kind of boundary judgment call this file has made before (e.g. Coco Tang at the Deansgate/Spinningfields line); flagged for the reviewer, but the coordinate is closer to this district's own centroid and existing venues (Manchester Art Gallery, Bar Shrimp) than to any neighbouring district's. Reuses the existing ART GALLERY type. Moderate-high confidence — nearly 60 years of continuous trading under the same gallery name, well-documented, current published hours, no closure signals.
